query: Automotive parts substantial transformation country of origin CBP

statements.text: So, if you are sourcing inputs from China, and transforming them into a finished product in a Mexico, then Mexico will likely be the country of origin for the product.
Many US Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) stipulate the precise amount of inputs that must be from the country in question in order to qualify for a special, lower (usually zero percent) duty rate.

December 7, 2016 : CIT: Energizer Battery v. US, Slip Op. 16-116: The CIT holds a simple assembly of flashlights is insufficient for justify a substantial transformation of the goods for Country of Origin purposes.
Pursuant to 19 C.F.R. § 134.1(b), Customs will generally consider the 2nd country to be the country of origin only if those inputs underwent “substantial transformation” there.

Per CBP rulings including N357277 on control arms, simple assembly operations do not result in substantial transformation. The character remains the country of origin of the inputs that gave the product its essential identity.

Anti-circumvention enforcement targets importers claiming non-China origin on products that are essentially Chinese-component assembly to avoid Section 301 tariffs. CBP enforcement has tightened in response to large-scale China relocation through Southeast Asia, with case-by-case substantial transformation analysis used to disallow optimistic origin claims.

January 23, 2020: CBP: Substantial Transformation: H303864 dated December 26, 2019 and concerning automotive windshield wiper pumps, where Customs rules against a substantial transformation in Mexico using Energizer Battery.

USMCA preference applies to qualifying goods that meet specific tariff shift or regional value content rules. The country where the qualifying transformation occurs (Mexico, Canada, or U.S.) is the country of origin for preference purposes, with 0% MFN duty rate on qualifying entries.
July 6, 2018: LIST 1 section 301 tariffs go into effect, creating an incentive for importers to move complex assembly operations out of China for COO purposes.
If your goods do not meet the criteria for “substantial transformation” – you may be incorrectly identifying the country of origin, which is a serious violation of U.S. law.

The 2026 CBP ruling N357277 on control arms confirmed that assembly of components does not result in substantial transformation, and the character of the control arms remained the ball joint assembly's origin.
CBP enforcement on substantial transformation has tightened in response to large-scale China relocation through Southeast Asia.
